title: CI evidence (advisory, unauthenticated)
description: Machine-readable evidence about one commit: what the established base revision's rules say about the change, and what GitHub reports about the CI run. It is data for a reviewer or an orchestrator, produced by a tool that must be run from a trusted place; it is not a signed attestation.

collector.description: Who produced the document. All of it is a claim.

tool.description: The tool that produced this document.

tool_source.description: Where the tool's code came from. A claim.

trust.description: Trust declaration. The consumer must obtain the data from GitHub itself and run the tool itself.

level.description: A file cannot prove where it came from.

authenticated_by_github.description: Nothing in this file is signed or attested by GitHub.

trusted_base.description: Present when a base revision was given.

anyOf.description: Result of judging the change with the base revision's rules.

tool.description: The tool that judged the change.

trusted_logic.description: Where the rules came from: always the base revision.

file_count.description: Files of validation logic read from the base.

manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the names and contents of those files.

anchor.description: Where the caller says this ran. A claim, never proof.

anchor_is_claim.description: The anchor is declared by whoever invoked the tool and is not verified.

truncated.description: Whether the list below is shorter than the total.

items.description: One changed path, classified by the base policy.

class.description: Risk class under the base policy.

categories.description: Risk categories under the base policy.

flags.description: Facts about which control files changed.

ops_code_changed.description: Anything under ops/ changed (validator, checker, tests).

build_inputs_changed.description: A file that changes what lint, type check or build do changed.

link_or_submodule_added.description: A symbolic link or submodule was added.

control_plane_paths.description: Changed paths that are control-plane under the base policy.

protected_paths.description: Changed paths that are protected, control-plane or immutable.

ci_entrypoints_changed.description: A script that CI or its npm hooks run changed.

rules.description: The base revision's validator applied to the head: first with the base's policy and schemas, then with the head's own policy.

head_data_under_base_policy.description: One run of the base revision's validator.

ok.description: Whether the validator reported no errors.

truncated.description: Whether more errors exist than are listed.

head_policy_under_base_validator.description: One run of the base revision's validator.

ok.description: Whether the validator reported no errors.

truncated.description: Whether more errors exist than are listed.

task_scope.description: Present only when a task id was given.

anyOf.description: Task scope as recorded in the base revision.

source.description: Where the task scope came from.

human_review_required.description: A human must review before this is accepted.

enforcement.description: Always advisory: nothing in this document enforces anything.

github_ci.description: Present when GitHub run data was supplied.

anyOf.description: What GitHub reports about the run, read without trusting the run.

workflow_run.description: The workflow run as GitHub reports it.

anyOf.description: owner/name of the repository the head commit lives in.

checks.description: Present only when check runs were supplied.

anyOf.description: Check runs for the evaluated commit.
Slug of the app that reported the check.

token_permissions.description: Present only when a job log was supplied.

anyOf.description: Token permissions printed in the job log.

test_evidence.description: Present only when a job log was supplied.

anyOf.description: Test and validation evidence parsed from the log.

authority.description: The log is printed by code from the branch under test; only the step conclusion is GitHub's own statement.

consistency.description: Checks that the pieces describe the same commit, workflow and steps.

blocking.description: Whether a failure makes ci_passed false.

verdict.description: Deterministic conclusions from the sections above. Advisory. Documents written by the earlier version of the tool lack missing_evidence and are still accepted; consumers must treat their evidence_complete as weaker.

timestamp.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp with second precision and a trailing Z.

verdict.description: Deterministic conclusions from the sections above. Advisory. This is the current shape: it always lists the mandatory inputs that were not supplied.

ci_passed.description: Null only when no GitHub run data was supplied. False when GitHub's data shows a failure or an inconsistency, and also when a mandatory check could not run because its input (check runs, job log) was missing: not established as passed is not passed.

anyOf.description: Every blocking check ran and held, and the run succeeded.

ci_trust_basis.description: Whether CI's own definition (workflow, ops code, policy, schemas, package scripts, build inputs) is the base's. If not, the CI result is not evidence.

human_review_required.description: A human must review before this is accepted.

evidence_complete.description: Every mandatory input was supplied (trusted-base check, GitHub run and job data, check runs, job log), every mandatory check ran, and no blocking check failed.

missing_evidence.description: The mandatory inputs that were not supplied, in a fixed order; empty only when everything was supplied.

items.description: An input a complete assessment needs.

reasons.description: Why a human is required or the evidence is incomplete.

verdict_before_missing_evidence.description: A verdict written by an earlier version of the tool, before missing_evidence existed. It stays valid so that stored evidence is not invalidated. In such a document evidence_complete only says that a trusted-base section and GitHub data were present and consistent; it does not say that check runs and a job log were present.

ci_passed.description: Null when no CI data was supplied.

anyOf.description: Every blocking check held and the run succeeded.

ci_trust_basis.description: Whether CI's own definition (workflow, ops code, policy, schemas, package scripts, build inputs) is the base's. If not, the CI result is not evidence.

human_review_required.description: A human must review before this is accepted.

evidence_complete.description: Both the trusted-base check and the GitHub data are present and consistent.

reasons.description: Why a human is required or the evidence is incomplete.
